description: Photon Pirates is a team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge, our first hackathon. We are motivated by a shared interest in space science and technology, and we aim to apply open NASA data to build a practical, well-researched solution.Our approach is built on rapid iteration, clear communication, and a focus on real-world impact. We combine technical skills with creative problem-solving, and we are committed to delivering a working prototype within the challenge timeline.As first-time participants, we bring fresh perspectives and a strong drive to learn, collaborate, and contribute meaningfully to the Space Apps community.
summary:
Surveyor 3: The Robot Who Waited is an interactive digital storybook I created as part of  Team Photon Pirates for the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.”

My project brings the story of NASA's Surveyor 3 lunar lander to life through 15 pages of visual, interactive storytelling. Launched in 1967, Surveyor 3 explored the lunar surface, captured thousands of images and conducted soil experiments before losing contact with Earth. More than two years later, Apollo 12 astronauts visited the lander and recovered components for scientific study.

Through historical NASA imagery, animations, interactive navigation and mission facts, I transform the story of this abandoned spacecraft into an engaging learning experience.

My project addresses the challenge by showing that discarded space equipment is more than forgotten machinery: it carries scientific discoveries, engineering achievements and stories worth preserving. I aim to make space exploration history accessible, engaging and memorable.

Team: Photon Pirates
details:
Project Details – Surveyor 3: The Robot Who Waited

Surveyor 3: The Robot Who Waited is an interactive digital storybook I developed as part of Team Photon Pirates for NASA Space Apps Challenge. It tells the true story of NASA’s Surveyor 3 lunar lander, which explored the Moon in 1967 and was later visited by Apollo 12 astronauts.

The project works as a 15-page interactive experience. Users can navigate through the story, explore mission events, and discover Surveyor 3’s cameras, soil-sampling equipment, scientific experiments, and eventual recovery by Apollo 12. It includes interactive animations, navigation controls, visual transitions, and a responsive design for desktop and mobile devices.

The main benefit is making space exploration history easier and more engaging to understand. Instead of presenting mission facts as a traditional article, the storybook helps users connect with the spacecraft and understand the scientific value of equipment that remains on the Moon. Its intended impact is to encourage curiosity about space exploration and preserve the stories and discoveries behind NASA’s abandoned equipment.

I developed the project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Visual Studio Code for coding and GitHub Pages for hosting. I also used Canva to create the project presentation and incorporated historical imagery from official NASA sources.

The creative element is its storytelling approach: Surveyor 3 is presented almost like a character whose journey, work, silence, and unexpected reunion with Apollo 12 unfold page by page. I combined factual information with interactive elements to make the experience memorable while keeping the historical content grounded in NASA sources.

During development, I considered historical accuracy, ease of navigation, accessibility, mobile responsiveness, image loading, and the balance between storytelling and scientific information. My goal was to make the story accessible to a wide audience while respecting the real mission and its legacy.

Team: Photon Pirates
